notes: Checked against OpenIntro's License page and Terms of Use. The licence page puts the Statistics textbooks under CC BY-SA 3.0, which on its own would let a paid app show a passage with credit. It's link only for now, because the Terms of Use add two things the owner has to weigh. First, users may not "harvest data from the website" for anything unrelated to OpenIntro or for commercial purposes, and must ask OpenIntro first if that is ambiguous for their purpose; the clause sits in the section on personal information, but its wording isn't limited to it. Second, a "website scraping agreement" claims stock or payments from any company that takes content from openintro.org by automated means to train an AI or ML system. So no tool or agent of Ceder's should fetch openintro.org content, the bank's agents never read it, and showing it would at least need the book taken by hand from a file that carries the licence. Other limits even under the licence: OpenIntro's name, logo, covers and website aren't licensed, a derivative can't use an OpenIntro title or look like an OpenIntro product, files without a licence notice aren't open, and slides may hold images under other licences or fair use. Partner Program books on the site aren't OpenIntro's. Nothing from it goes into the bank.
